en: A Brief Ritual for the Practice and Recitation of the Mahākaruṇā-hṛdaya Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master from Northern India, the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra,
under Imperial Decree during the Tang Dynasty.
Based on the *Abhiṣeka-maṇḍala-sūtra*,
this explains the dharma-gate for practicing dhāraṇīs,
seeking swift deliverance from the great ocean of birth and death.
One who wishes to swiftly realize unsurpassed bodhi must first enter the consecration maṇḍala of the ocean-like assembly of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
having received the consecration, they should give rise to a heart of joy.
Having personally received the rules for recitation from one's teacher,
it is best to subsequently practice in a pure room, a mountain forest, or by flowing water—
these being the most excellent locations.
Having established the maṇḍala and installed the principal deity,
the practitioner of mantras should face the east and smear the ground with *gomaya*.
Grind white sandalwood incense into a fragrant paste and use it to smear the altar,
whether square or circular, and of whatever size one desires.
Then, scatter flowers and burn incense upon the altar as an offering.
Take two pure vessels, fill them completely with scented water,
and place them within the altar for the purpose of making offerings.
Whether the practitioner bathes or does not bathe, there is no obstacle whatsoever.
One should simply direct the mind toward contemplation and observation that the fundamental nature of all sentient beings is pure.
Being obscured by adventitious defilements,
one does not perceive the pure *dharmatā* of *tathatā*; therefore,
for the sake of purifying it, [one practices].
One should recite this mantra with a sincere heart three or seven times. The mantra is:
Oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāvaśuddho ’haṃ. By the empowerment of this mantra, [the purification is accomplished].
Having attained complete purity of body, speech, and mind,
one then places the five limbs upon the ground and pays homage with devotion to all Buddhas and great Bodhisattvas of the ten directions throughout the vast Mahāyāna.
Kneeling with the right knee on the ground, one performs repentance, rejoices in merit, requests [the turning of the wheel], and makes vows.
Taking refuge in the Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions, the most excellent Dharma, and the assembly of Bodhisattvas,
I pay respectful homage with body, speech, and mind through pure actions, bowing with palms joined in earnest devotion.
Whatever sins have been produced by the actions of body, speech, and mind throughout the beginningless cycle of existence within the various realms of being—
just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have confessed them, so do I now present my confession. Furthermore,
regarding the merit produced by the three vajra-actions within the practices and aspirations of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas:
I rejoice in all the roots of virtue accumulated by the Pratyekabuddhas, Śrāvakas, and sentient beings.

To all the Lamps of the World seated at the site of enlightenment, whose awakening-eye has blossomed to illuminate the three realms of existence, I now kneel and first entreat you: turn the unsurpassed, wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
To all the Tathāgatas, lords of the triple world, who are approaching parinirvāṇa without remainder,
I entreat you all to remain for a long time, not abandoning your compassionate vows to save the world.
Through this confession, entreaty, and sympathetic joy in merit, may I never lose the bodhicitta.
Amidst the sublime assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, you are always a virtuous friend, never wearying of or abandoning them.
Born free from the eight difficulties, you possess the marks of wisdom regarding past lives to adorn your body;
far removed from ignorance, you are endowed with compassion and wisdom, and are able to fully perfect all the pāramitās.
Born into noble lineages with abundant wealth and prosperity, With vast retinues that are ever-prosperous,
Possessing the four unhindered analytical knowledges and ten masteries, And the six supernormal powers and all meditative absorptions fully perfected—
Just as with Vajradhvaja and Samantabhadra, May this dedication through praise be likewise.
Next, the mantra for prostrating to the principal deity and the assembly of holy beings is as follows:
Oṃ praṇamāmi. By means of this mantra, one performs prostration.
The assembly of the honored deities accepts [the practitioner] as their sovereign.
Next, one sits before the honored deity in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka) or the half-lotus posture (ardhaparyaṅka),
giving rise to a mind of great compassion and thinking, "I shall practice this dharma."
In order that all sentient beings may swiftly emerge from the great ocean of birth and death and quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment,
one should first grind various fragrances and use them to anoint the hands.
Thereafter, one binds the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family.
With both hands joined in the hollowed *añjali*,
one extends the two index fingers and bends them to support the upper joints of the two middle fingers.
Bend both thumbs and support the lower joints of the two index fingers;
the seal is thus formed.
Place the seal at the heart.
Visualize the Tathāgata’s thirty-two major marks and eighty minor signs with such clarity and distinctness that it is as if they were before one's eyes.
Recite the mantra seven times with a sincere mind.
The mantra is: Oṃ tathāgatodbhavāya svāhā. By means of this mudrā and the recitation of this mantra, one immediately awakens all the Tathāgatas.
May you all protect, mindfully regard, and empower the practitioner;
by touching my body with your light,
may all my karmic obstacles and hindrances be utterly extinguished.
One's lifespan shall be extended and merit increased;
the holy assembly of the Buddha Family will protect one with joy.
In birth after birth, one shall be free from all evil realms.
One will be born through transformation from a lotus and swiftly realize unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family.
Join the two hands with palms hollowed together;
extend the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers,
and bend them into the shape of a lotus flower.
Place the seal of peace at the heart.
Visualize Avalokiteśvara as fully endowed with all the marks and signs of excellence.
Recite the mantra seven times and release the seal over the right side of the crown of the head.
The mantra is: Oṃ padmanābha svāhā. By means of this mudrā and the recitation of this mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
Immediately, Avalokiteśvara and the other members of the Lotus Family of all Bodhisattvas, having awakened,
were all filled with joy and bestowed their empowerment, protection, and mindfulness.
The light of all bodhisattvas shines upon and touches their bodies,
whereby all karmic obstructions are completely eliminated.
All bodhisattvas constantly act as their virtuous friends.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Vajra Family:
turn the palm of the left hand outward,
and place the back of the right palm upon the back of the left palm.
Using the left and right thumbs and little fingers,
interlace the hands in the shape of a vajra;
place the seal at the heart.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi and recite the mantra seven times, scattering [the offerings] over the left side of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vāruṇa-pāśaya svāhā. By means of this mudrā and the recitation of this mantra, one awakens the noble assembly of the Vajra family.
All Vajradharas shall empower and protect [him].
All karmic obstructions and hindrances will be entirely extinguished.
No suffering whatsoever shall touch his body.
One shall then attain a body as firm and solid as a vajra.
Next, bind the Samaya Mudrā for protecting the body:
interlace the hands with the palms facing inward, placing the right hand over the left.
Hold the tips of the two middle fingers together.
Bend the two index fingers into the shape of hooks,
ensuring they do not touch the backs of the middle fingers.
Pressing the two thumbs against the two ring fingers,
the seal is thus formed;
it is applied to five locations on the body.
That is to say: at the forehead, then the left and right shoulders, then the heart and throat;
finally, perform the mudrā of scattering above the crown of the head, reciting the mantra once for each.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajrāṅgi-pratipātaya svāhā. By binding this mudrā and reciting this mantra with empowerment, [the purpose is accomplished].
One immediately becomes clad in the adamantine armor (*vajrakavaca*).
All *vināyakas* and various obstructing māras retreat and flee in all directions.
One clearly perceives that the practitioner’s body is enveloped in radiance, and their majestic power (*vibhūti*) is sovereign and autonomous.
Whether dwelling in mountain forests or facing perilous difficulties, they shall be entirely without fear.
Regarding all calamities such as water and fire, all manner of misfortunes,
tigers, wolves, lions, blades, staves, shackles, and fetters— [they shall be free from them].
All such matters as these will be entirely extinguished, bringing joy to those who behold them.
After the end of life, they shall not fall into the evil realms,
but shall instead be born in the pure and wondrous lands of all Buddhas.
Next, having bound the great mudrā of the Great Bodhisattva Vajracakra’s Great Majestic Power,
those who enter the maṇḍala receive the three types of unobstructed discipline pertaining to the three times.
Upon entering the maṇḍala, one is fully endowed with the samaya and unconditioned prohibitions (avajñā-saṃvara) numbering as many as the atoms within the worlds of ten dust-motes of Buddha-fields.
This applies even to such acts as bending the body, looking up or down, speaking, exhaling, or giving rise to thoughts and mental activities.
If one has forgotten or neglected the bodhicitta and fallen away from the roots of virtue,
one can eliminate transgressions and faults by reciting and attending to this mudrā, mantra, and sublime skillful means.
The samaya, as before, becomes doubly radiant;
because it can purify body, speech, and mind,
one thereby achieves entry into all maṇḍalas.
Having received the initiation and the samaya,
one should form the mudrā and recite the mantra seven times.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Erect the two concentrations;
bind the two concentrations with two mindfulnesses;
extend the two wisdoms side by side and straighten them.
Rest it securely within the heart.
Recite it seven times with a sincere mind.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namo siddhye vidyānām | sarvatathāgatānām | am | viraji viraji | mahākrodhavajri | sata sata | sarati sarati | trātrai trātrai | vidhamani | samantajvālini | trāmati siddha | giridraṃ | svāhā.* While reciting this mantra, one should form this visualization: Namo siddhye vidyānām. To all the Tathāgatas. Am! O you who possess the vajra of the great wrathful one, you who purify, you who purify! You who are present, you who are present! You who traverse, you who traverse! O protector, O protector! O you who shatter [obstacles]! O you who blaze with universal radiance! O you who bring relief! O you who are perfected! O you who are the mountain-peak! Svāhā! While reciting this mantra, one should perform this mental visualization.
May all sentient beings within the six realms of cyclic existence, throughout the entirety of space and the pervasive realm of phenomena,
swiftly enter the great maṇḍala of the Universal Assembly and become equal to the Noble Ones.
Next, bind the seal of concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*) and enter the contemplation of the four immeasurable minds (*catur-apramāṇa*).
First, enter the meditative absorption of the immeasurable mind of loving-kindness (*maitry-apramāṇa-samādhi*),
universally taking all beings as objects with a fervent and pure mind.
All sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth possess the Tathāgatagarbha and are endowed with the threefold vajras of body, speech, and mind;
by the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets, [may they be purified].
Having contemplated in this way: "May all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra."
Then he recited the mantra of the Mahākaruṇā-samādhi:
Oṃ mahā-maitrya sphara. Next, he entered the samādhi of the wisdom of immeasurable compassion.
With a heart of compassion, one universally takes as objects all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth,
who are submerged in the ocean of suffering of saṃsāra.
Failing to awaken to one's own mind,
they give rise to false discrimination and various afflictions and karmic actions.
Consequently, they do not realize that True Suchness is equal to space.
May I give rise to merits as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
by the power of my cultivation of the three secrets and their empowerment,
may all sentient beings [attain this].
Having visualized oneself as being identical to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha,
one then recites the mantra of the Great Compassion Samādhi, which says:
Oṃ mahākāruṇikāya svāhā. Next, enter the samādhi of immeasurable sympathetic joy (muditā) and, with a pure mind, take all things as the object of focus.
All sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth are primordially pure like a lotus flower;
unstained by adventitious defilements, their intrinsic nature is pure.
By the power of the merit from my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Having observed in this way, one should then recite the mantra of the Samādhi of Great Joy:
Oṃ jñānapramodana svāhā. This is the wisdom of the samādhi of the immeasurable mind of equanimity.
With a mind of equanimity, one universally takes as objects all sentient beings of the six realms and four modes of birth,
who are all free from the notion of "mine" and free from the aggregates and elements.
Furthermore, being free from the grasper and the grasped, all phenomena are equal;
for the mind is fundamentally unborn, its nature and characteristics being empty.
This is by the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets.
Having contemplated in this way: "May all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha."
Then he recited the mantra of the Great Relinquishment Samādhi, saying:
Oṃ māhūbje kṣe sphāraja. This is the mantra for the practitioner.
By practicing the meditative concentrations of the four immeasurables and reciting the mantras,
all various demonic obstacles and karmic hindrances of humans and devas are completely eliminated,
and immeasurable merit and wisdom are instantaneously accumulated.
With body and mind made supple, pliant, and masterful,
one next forms the seal of the maṇḍala wheel:
both hands form vajra-fists.
With the powers of diligence, generosity, and wisdom mutually entwined,
seal the mouth while reciting the mantra;
one will thereby enter all maṇḍalas.
Next, place it upon the crown.
At the site where the maṇḍala has been established,
everything becomes a great maṇḍala.
Just as the *iṣṭadevatā* personally establishes the maṇḍala, the mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-cakra hūṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. By binding this mudrā and reciting the mantra for empowerment, [the rite is accomplished].
Even if a practitioner should transgress the Dharma,
erring in the three karmas and violating the samaya,
the precepts are able to eliminate all such faults, whereby everything becomes perfectly complete.
Next, perform the mudrā for inviting the principal deity:
interlace the two hands with palms facing inward to form fists,
and insert the left thumb into the palm.
With the right thumb, beckon [it] toward oneself.
The mantra is: Oṃ aruke ihi ihi svāhā. By means of the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, [the deity is summoned].
The Honored Deity Bodhisattva, not transgressing their original vow,
shall lead the assembly of sages to attend the site of practice,
bestowing empowerment so that the practitioner may swiftly fulfill their fundamental aspiration.
Next, form the mudrā of the Horse-Headed Vidyārāja to expel obstructors and establish the boundary:
join the two hands in *añjali*,
then bend the two index fingers and the two ring fingers.
With the palms facing upward and the nails pointing toward each other, extend the two thumbs apart;
this constitutes the seal. Rotate it to the left three times.
Visualizing that all obstructors are expelled,
the demons, spirits, and vināyakas retreat and flee in all directions.
Rotate the mudrā three times clockwise and then wave it up and down.
This immediately establishes the firm great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*). The mantra is:
Oṃ amṛtodbhavā hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, offer the arghya perfumed water with the mudrā.
With both hands, hold the arghya vessel filled with fragrant water and floating seasonal flowers;
offer it to the forehead.
The mantra is: *maṃsa maḥ svāhā*. By offering this arghya perfumed water, the three karmas of the practitioner are purified.
One washes away all afflictions, karmic offenses, and impurities.
From the stage of practice through aspiration up to the tenth stage and the stage of the Tathāgata,
when one realizes such stages and perfections (pāramitās), [one attains them].
One receives the consecration upon the head with the nectar-water of the Dharma from all Tathāgatas.
Next, one forms the mudrā for offering the seat:
join the two hands in the lotus-anjali gesture.
Extend the two ring fingers,
bending their tips so that they resemble the shape of an opening lotus flower.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kamala svāhā. By virtue of the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, the assembly of deities truly accepts [the offering] and sits upon the precious lotus throne.
Next, form the seal of universal offering:
join the two hands in *añjali* with the fingers slightly interlaced;
place the right hand over the left and position it upon the heart.
Recite the mantra five times.
From the mudrā, there flow forth oceans of clouds of various offerings:
unguents, flower garlands, incense, food, and drink.
With lamps, precious vases, celestial music, and exquisite performances,
universally make offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and the assembly of honored deities.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namoḥ sarvatathāgatebhyo viśvamukhebhyaḥ | svāhā | khaṃ | oṃ āgaccha sāṃprataṃ he am āgacchāñjanasvāhā*. By means of the empowerment of this mantra and mudrā, [the deity is summoned].
All the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and assemblies of honored deities receive truly vast offerings,
for this is established by the very nature of reality.
Next, recite the hymn of praise.

Next, bind the heart-secret mudrā of the Honored One. In accordance with the instructions, perform the recitation while clearly visualizing the physical marks and signs of the Honored One’s body, which radiates immeasurable great light in all directions.
May all classes of sentient beings who suffer, upon being touched by the light, attain peace and happiness.
Having recited the root mantra seven times, perform the *mudrā* of scattering [the flowers] from the crown of the head like hanging ribbons.
For the heart *mudrā*, join both palms together with the hollows of the hands facing inward.
Join the palms and move the two index fingers back and forth.
The mantra of the *Ārya-sahasrabhuja-sahasranetra-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-mahāsattva-vipula-paripūrṇa-apratihata-mahākaruṇā-citta-dhāraṇī* is as follows, according to the text.
Next, take up the rosary, hold it before you, and place it upon the crown of your head, consecrating it seven times with the mantra:
*Oṃ vilokana-māla svāhā*. Then, consecrate it seven times with the Thousand-Turn Mantra.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajraguhyarājaprasādaya hūṃ. Having performed this empowerment, one should immediately make this aspiration:
"May I and all sentient beings..."
May all sought-after supreme mundane and supramundane great vows be swiftly accomplished.
Holding the two hands with the beads at the heart,
recite the mantra once.
Accompanying the sound of the final syllable, move one bead at a time—
neither too slowly nor too quickly, neither too high nor too low—
pronouncing each syllable of the mantra so that it is distinct and clear.
Alternatively, perform *vajrajāpa*:
move the tip of the tongue slightly while keeping the lips and teeth closed,
remaining free from all distraction.
Focus the mind single-mindedly on the deity without allowing the attention to stray toward other forms.
Recite either a thousand or a hundred times, maintaining this count constantly.
When the recitation is finished, hold the rosary, prostrate with devotion, and make a sincere aspiration.
Returning to the original position, again bind the heart-secret mudrā of the Honored One and perform the recitation.
Disperse the mudrās as before.
Offer praise and make offerings with redoubled earnestness. Once more present the argha water while reciting the original vow.
Furthermore, using the seal of the Hayagrīva Vidyārāja, recite the mantra three times to dissolve the boundary as before.
Then, perform the seal for requesting the Honored One to descend and enter; with the thumbs drawn outward, form the seal for the mantra of dismissal, which is as follows:
Once the practitioner has escorted the noble assembly away, they should again form the mudrā of meditative concentration and arouse compassion;
empowered by the three families, they don the armor. Having completed the prostrations and taken leave, they may wander at will.
One who practices according to this method will swiftly gather merit and wisdom and attain the supernormal powers.
Attaining Entry into the Stage of Joy in the Present Life: A Brief Ritual for the Recitation and Practice of the Mahākaruṇā-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī Leading to Perfect Enlightenment after Sixteen Lifetimes.
